## What to download

You only need the files for the computers you use. The **Mac you want to control** needs the first file. To control it from **another computer**, either open your Heartfulness Remote web address in any browser (nothing to install), or install one of the client apps below.

### Heartfulness-Remote-Mac.zip: for the Mac you want to control
1. Click the file to download it, then double-click it in your Downloads folder to unzip it.
2. Open **README-FIRST.txt** and follow it. In short: drag **Heartfulness Remote** into your **Applications** folder and open it.
3. The first time, macOS says it can't check the app. Click **Done**, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**, then confirm. You only do this once.
4. Follow the setup window: allow **Screen Recording** and **Accessibility** when macOS asks.

### Heartfulness-Remote-Client-Mac.dmg: to control your Mac from another Mac
1. Double-click the file, then drag **Heartfulness Remote** onto the **Applications** folder.
2. Open it from Applications. The first time, use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, the same as above.
3. Type your Heartfulness Remote web address and sign in. Approve this new device from your phone or on your Mac.

### Heartfulness-Remote-Client-Windows-Setup.exe: to control your Mac from a Windows PC
1. Double-click the file. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click **More info → Run anyway**.
2. Follow the installer, then open **Heartfulness Remote** from the Start menu.
3. Type your Heartfulness Remote web address and sign in. Approve this new device from your phone or on your Mac.

### Heartfulness-Remote-Client-Windows.msi: the same Windows app as an MSI package
Use this one only if your IT person asks for an MSI. Everyone else should use the Setup.exe above. You never need both.

### SHA256SUMS.txt: optional
Fingerprints of the files above, so a technical helper can check that the downloads are exactly what was built. You can ignore it.

---
These apps are signed for personal use, not by Apple or Microsoft. That is why your computer asks you to confirm them the first time.
